recipes.name: Slow Cooker Lancaster County Pork and Sauerkraut

steps.text: Cut pork loin, if necessary, to fit in the slow cooker. Season with caraway seeds, and salt and pepper to taste. Pour sauerkraut over the roast.
Cook on High for 1 hour, then cook on Low for 5 to 6 hours. Internal temperature of the roast should be at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Lancaster County Pork and Sauerkraut
raw_recipe.description: What could be more effortless than pork, sauerkraut, and a handful of caraway seeds cooked for hours for a hearty, down home meal on New Year's Day.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Lancaster County Pork and Sauerkraut

recipeInstructions.text: Cut pork loin, if necessary, to fit in the slow cooker. Season with caraway seeds, and salt and pepper to taste. Pour sauerkraut over the roast.
Cook on High for 1 hour, then cook on Low for 5 to 6 hours. Internal temperature of the roast should be at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

review.reviewBody: Wow! This is definitely a New Year's Day tradition. Being from Pennsylvania, I had to make this. It was excellent. I took one 16 oz. bag of Boar's Head Sauerkraut and layered that on the bottom. Then sprinkled some of the caraway seeds and put the pork in with some salt, pepper, and a little brown sugar. I cut up a large granny smith apple and put that over the pork and then added the other bag of sauerkraut and sprinkled some more caraway seeds. I added just a little bit of water and set the crock pot on low for 8 hours. The pork was falling apart. It went great with Suzy's Mashed Red Potatoes and some sweet peas and for dessert Nutty Apple Crisp.

I had everything on hand to make this dish. My pressure cooker does not have a sauté feature so I browned the pork in a bit of olive oil and butter on the stove. I then placed the pork on the sliced onions in the pressure cooker. I deglazed the sauté pan with a bit of the cranberry mixture, placed that on the pork and a few minutes later a perfect roast with a yummy sauce. I omitted the tarragon only as a personal preference - just a taste for which I do not care. Thank you for sharing a recipe that is quick, delicious and easy.

I first had a similar dish while living in Harrisburg, PA several years ago on New Years Day at a local fire hall. Back in the south we always had ham hocks and black eyed peas on New Years Day. I was glad to find this recipe because it’s absolutely delicious! I did as others have suggested and added a Granny Smith Apple and some brown sugar. I layered the bottom of the slow cooker with 16oz of sauerkraut and sprinkled with Caraway seeds, added the loin, salt and pepper, brown sugar, topped with slices of apple, another 16oz of sauerkraut, and sprinkled with more Caraway seeds. I cooked a 3lb loin on high for three hours and then on low for five more. It was fall apart tender and absolutely perfect!

I used a Boston Butt roast because I think its a better cut to use in a crockpot since it doesn't get as dry when cooking. I salt and peppered the roast after searing. Then I poured 3 cups of water, 2 tsp of chicken bullion and 1 tsp of beef bullion from Pensky's as well as 3/4 c of dark beer over the roast in the crockpot. Once the roast was halfway done I removed half of the broth to use for gravy. After that, I added the drained sauerkraut and a couple of sliced apples to continue cooking. (Sauerkraut plus roast broth doesn't make the best gravy lol) Served with mashed potatoes, gravy, and steamed broccoli.

My family is from Lancaster County and we were raised on this dish. I make it exactly as is written with one exception. I always use pork shoulder/butt. Why use an expensive cut of pork? This can also be made on top of the stove cooking on low for 2 to 3 hours depending on weight.

If I could give this recipe 6 stars, I would. This was absolutely terrific. The timing is perfect on this recipe. It was moist, and melt in your mouth, and the caraway seed flavor was great. I followed what a few others suggested by adding 2 granny smith apples, peeled, cored and sliced into 1/8ths for the last 2 hours and added 2-3 tbls of brown sugar, and I added 1 teasoon of thyme, and doubled the caraway seeds. I cooked this today on New Year's Day 2018, served with roasted garlic mashed potatoes, cherry pie and Blue Bell Vanilla Ice Cream..........This is a keeper, thank you so much for a wonderful recipe.

Simply divine!!! It's a real KEEPER and I will make it this way every New Year's Day from now on. It was soooo good that my husband and I ate leftovers this morning for breakfast and he is already looking forward to leftovers for lunch!

I used about 3 pounds of boneless pork tenderloin, one 32 ounce jar of sauerkraut with juice, a pinch of salt and pepper, and 1 teaspoon caraway seeds. I also took the advice of other viewers and added 2 peeled and sliced Granny Smith apples and 2 tablespoons of brown sugar. I cooked it on high in the crock pot for 1 hour and 15 minutes and then turned it down to low for 7 hours. The pork was so tender and moist and the sauerkraut had just the right amount of sweet/sour taste to it.

I served this dish with mashed potatoes, a side of homemade veggie soup, and a garden salad. For dessert I made baked cinnamon apples and served with a scoop of french vanilla ice cream! It was a BIG HIT!

I made this with a modification. In a bowl, I pre-mixed the sauerkraut with salt, pepper, 1/4 cup dark brown sugar, and a heaping tablespoon of molasses. Then piled the mixture on top of the pork in a slow cooker.
* Everyone loved it, including the kids

Put pork loin (not tenderloin) in slow cooker (cover in spices), added a pack of Bob Evan regular sausages, then added sauerkraut on top. Cooked on high for 1 hour, then low for another 5 to 6 hours. Excellent and easy!

My favorite meal. I serve it over mashed potatoes like many other reviewers. I put 1 peeled Granny Smith apple and a small Vidalia onion in the food processor and mix that with the sauerkraut (I used the refrigerated bag of sauerkraut) I stir in a handful of caraway seeds and 1/4 cup brown sugar. Then I place the pork on top of the sauerkraut (I love how the pork juices melt into the sauerkraut). This time I used boneless country style spare ribs. I salted, peppered, shook on a little onion powder and spread a little more brown sugar over the meat. Crock pot on low 6-8 hours. Yum
Additions: Sliced onion, 2 tbsp Brown sugar, 2 tbsp BBQ sauce, 2 apples cored and cut in 8s. Apples go on top. Cook high 4 hours low 4 hours.

We did a garlic sauerkraut and a classic sauerkraut with caraway seeds. Added onion and apple (not sure the apple was all that necessary but so many people in the comments said to add it). Husband shredded up the pork and mixed it all together. Delicious. Next time we will add more sauerkraut.
Made as directed only double the sauce. Will try adding apples next time. Easy and delish
When you're from Lancaster County that's what you do!! Have been serving for over 60 yrs. So easy to make and serve. What's not to like!!
being from Lancaster- no seeds- liquid is flat beer that is opened the night before -and left on the counter overnight. apple slices are optional since the sides are mashed potatoes and applesauce.
Tender and delicious! I added apple chunks and onions

I'm originally from Chicago where there is a high Polish population, so finding good ethnic food is easy. Now that we live in rural Colorado, ethnic food is hard to find. This recipe is great. I added 2 apples, 2T brown sugar and turkey kielbasa. It tasted fantastic. Next time I'd double the sauerkraut and caraway.
This was a big hit with my family!
How can you go wrong with sauerkraut and pork.
Will definitely make again and will add more sauerkraut. Recipe doesn't call for enough!
